title: Ai Mcp End to End
description: Get the semio ai mcp server (semio-os-mcp, the `semio` entry in .mcp.json) working end to end: plugin/app/artifact-independent with progressive enhancement, so an agent can read artifacts, inferences and ui information, invoke ui actions, call mutations and traverse history over a live or headless workspace.
summary:
Finished the semio OS MCP gateway (`semio-os-mcp`, the `semio` entry in .mcp.json) end to end: plugin/app/artifact-independent, progressively enhanced, and verified against the real compiled binary.

SURFACE — retired `DECLARED_STUB_TOOL_NAMES` entirely. `tools/list` is now 22 tools with zero stubs, pinned by `GATEWAY_TOOL_NAMES` and asserted against the live registry: 3 core gateway, 8 mutation-protocol, 5 artifact, 2 inference, 4 ui/job. Added 5 bilingual (EN/DE) protocol-teaching prompts, replacing the empty prompt registry.

PLUGIN INDEPENDENCE — the production catalog was a hardcoded note+cad fixture; it now compiles from the real installed plugin registry (new registry facet), never falling back to fixture data. RoutingArtifactChannel resolves the owning plugin per capability, replacing first a hardcoded "note" literal and then a single-plugin-only resolver. No plugin id appears anywhere in the gateway.

NEW CAPABILITIES — real artifact_* tools; inference access via inference_list/inference_get and semio://artifact/{id}/inference[/{field}]; UI information and UI actions over the existing shell bridge plus plugin-agnostic job_get/job_cancel; a workspace-backed ResourceRegistry so the workspace's own resources (previously dead code behind CatalogResourceRegistry) actually reach clients; real mutation round-trips through PluginArtifactChannel replacing blanket channel.not-wired rejections, and deletion of a hardcoded {"valid": true} validation response.

PROGRESSIVE ENHANCEMENT — three tiers (bare / headless via --folder|--hub / attached via a shell on /bridge). A tool's presence in tools/list and a resource's in resources/list never depends on tier; only results do, as typed retryable PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE naming the exact missing binding. A late-bound BridgeSlot lets the tool registry resolve the bridge the HTTP transport mints after the server is built, without a second worker pool.

TWO LIVE PRODUCTION BUGS FOUND AND FIXED — (1) HeadlessWorkspace never drained its artifact stores, so a --folder-bound server would panic at shutdown on the store's terminal-empty assert; fixed with a real Drop that installs the store's own canonical disposer and drains to terminal. (2) A real plugin registry combined with a single-plugin-only resolver meant every mutation failed on any real install — invisible at fixture scale, since a 1-plugin and a 2-plugin catalog both satisfy a resolver that accepts exactly one.

TWO GATES THAT READ GREEN WHILE MEASURING NOTHING — the conformance harness resolved its binary against a retired ticket's scratch dir, so all three suites had been silently skipping themselves (graduated to target/debug, honouring CARGO_TARGET_DIR/SEMIO_OS_MCP_BIN); and a legacy test named "prompts/list is empty" only ever asserted Array.isArray. Both were found by reading passing output, not failing output.

ALSO FIXED, PRE-EXISTING AND NOT OURS — BridgeAsyncState held 345KB of stack-allocated arrays, so any BridgeHandle::new() blew libtest's stack (the failing test name moved between runs); fixed with heap-allocated slot rings in bridge and transport.

VERIFIED — binary builds (46.8MB). vitest 33/33 against the real binary over stdio JSON-RPC, including 12 new end-to-end tests, none skipped: the 22-tool census, no tool self-describing as a stub, object-typed schemas, bilingual prompts, the resource families, all three tiers behaving differently, and the catalog proven not to be the fixture. Rust: workspace::quick 24/24, artifact::quick 9/9, bridge 40/40.

NOT VERIFIED — the full 284-test lib suite has not completed in one process. A 16-attempt/47-minute retry loop never found a compilable tree: peers are mid-flight on a framework-wide serde-removal migration, oscillating between semio-framework-replication and semio-framework-os-kernel. Cargo never reached the test binary (no aborts), so this is an unavailable tree, not evidence against the code. The transport half of the heap-ring fix is code-complete but not watched passing. DEFAULT_SESSION_ID remains process-fixed — fixing it needs a connection-aware McpServer, deliberately not attempted while nothing compiled.

Unblocking this ticket also required repairing peer-owned crates left broken by that migration: plugin-host (38 to 0), os-kernel/store (75 to 0), semio-framework workflow+run (166 to 0, 54/54 tests), and a bound-propagation residue in store/sync.
